register.name: Extended Credit Facility, 41 months
register.detail: IMF · Staff-level agreement announced 11 August 2026, Press Release No. 26/275 · 145% of quota · Board consideration was expected in September 2026, with the 2026 Article IV consultation
register.note: Subject to approval by IMF management and the Executive Board; the IMF release gives no dollar figure
register.text: A 41-month programme agreed at staff level after the 2026 Article IV mission, held from 16 to 29 June 2026. It aims to mobilise revenue, especially from mining, to finance priority spending while preserving debt sustainability, with human capital and jobs beyond mining among its priorities.

register.name: Country Partnership Framework FY27–FY33
register.detail: World Bank, IFC and MIGA · Endorsed 23 June 2026 · 2027 to 2033 · aligned with the national programme Simandou 2040
register.note: Public and private commitments over the period; an indicative initial three-year IDA21 allocation of about $471 million
register.text: The World Bank Group’s partnership with Guinea from 2027 to 2033, aligned with the national plan Simandou 2040: jobs, basic services and revenue management. IFC is to unlock private investment in agribusiness and other productive sectors, and MIGA to guarantee private investment in infrastructure and energy.

register.name: Skills for Innovation, Resilience and Aspirations (SIRA) Program, phase 1
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Approved 23 June 2026 · IDA credit of $100 million and a $2 million grant from the Early Learning Partnership trust fund · first phase of a ten-year programme
register.note: About 2.7 million young Guineans expected to benefit
register.text: Modernises secondary education and expands technical and vocational training, in agribusiness, energy and digital skills, with support for young entrepreneurs and job placement. It serves the education and livelihood standards, where 17.3% of children read a simple text by the end of primary school.

register.name: Commercial Agriculture Development Project, phase 2
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 23 June 2026 · AgriConnect as the anchor vehicle
register.note: About 66,000 jobs and 250,000 farmers and rural households by 2033; $150 million of private capital to be mobilised
register.text: Promotes commercial farming, attracts private investment and expands employment in key agricultural value chains. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Domestic Revenue Mobilization and Public Expenditure Management Project
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 23 June 2026 · revenue administration, public expenditure and debt management
register.note: Aims to raise the tax-to-GDP ratio from 12.1% to 15% by 2031
register.text: Strengthens the public finances of Guinea as it prepares to manage future revenues from Simandou. Domestic revenue is the public money that pays for the seven standards.

register.name: Emergency Response and Nafa Program Support Project (PRU-APN)
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · total IDA financing of $200 million · productive safety net
register.note: The World Bank country page does not state the approval date
register.text: Expands the productive safety net to respond to shocks and strengthen the resilience of vulnerable households, and promotes access to better jobs for vulnerable young people and women. It serves the livelihood and food standards, where 43.7% live below the national poverty line.

register.name: Guinea Electricity Access Scale-Up Project, phase 2 (PAAEG 2)
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Release of 30 June 2025 · IDA credit · total financing about $271.8 million, with $100 million of parallel co-financing from the European Investment Bank
register.note: About 1.53 million people to gain access, 960,022 of them for the first time
register.text: Connects households, businesses and public institutions under the national low-cost electricity access programme, with rural mini-grids run by private operators supported by IFC, and institutional reforms at Electricité de Guinée. It serves energy, the standard furthest from reach, where 53.8% have electricity.

register.name: Kounki Fisheries and Aquaculture Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Release of 6 June 2025 · IDA credit · $5 million PROBLUE grant · €20 million from the French Development Agency · €4 million from the France–Guinea Debt Reduction and Development Contract
register.note: The IDA credit; the PROBLUE grant and the French co-financing come on top
register.text: Strengthens climate resilience and develops value chains in fishing and aquaculture communities, with stronger fisheries and mangrove management and access to finance for small businesses in the sector. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: Guinea Water and Sanitation Project (PEAG)
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) · Release of 4 April 2025 · IDA credit · greater Conakry
register.note: 2,612,467 expected beneficiaries, 572,200 of them with drinking water for the first time
register.text: Finances the construction of water production and distribution infrastructure for the Conakry metropolitan area, and better latrines and hygiene teaching for students in 400 secondary schools. It serves the water and shelter standards, where 74.2% have basic drinking water.

register.name: Guinea Enhancing Health System Transformation (GUEST) Project
register.detail: World Bank (IDA) and the Global Financing Facility · Release dated 25 September 2024 · the second GFF grant to Guinea
register.note: Total of IDA and GFF financing; the split is not stated
register.text: Strengthens health facilities in staff, equipment, energy, water and medicines, with a focus on reproductive, maternal, newborn, child and adolescent health and nutrition, and free care for the extremely poor. It serves the health standard, where the WHO service coverage index is 43.

register.name: Emergency Response and Nafa Program Support Project (PRU-APN), additional financing
register.detail: Approved, release of 4 August 2025 · IDA additional financing · 120,000 vulnerable households in the programme
register.note: Continued support to current beneficiaries and stronger emergency response
register.text: Keeps support flowing to the households already in the Nafa safety net and strengthens the national response to crises and natural disasters. It serves food and livelihood.

register.name: Guinea–Senegal Road Corridor Construction Project
register.detail: Approved 15 December 2024 by the IsDB Board · financing signed 19 June 2025 · Labé–Mali towards Kédougou
register.note: The Guinean part of the corridor linking Labé and Mali with Kédougou in Senegal
register.text: Builds the road corridor that links the Fouta Djallon to Senegal, co-financed with the African Development Fund and BOAD. It serves livelihood, by opening markets for farmers and traders.

register.name: Siguiri Regional Hospital, Cissela–Banko–N’Dèma road and Tinkisso 2 hydropower
register.detail: Signed 10 September 2026, Conakry · three EBID loans · hospital €65.8 million · road €143.05 million · hydropower €60.6 million
register.note: A 200-bed regional hospital, 84 km of road and an 11 MW hydropower plant
register.text: Three loans from the ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development: a 200-bed hospital in Siguiri, 84 km of paved road and the 11 MW Tinkisso 2 plant of 48 GWh a year. They serve health, energy and livelihood.
by: ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development

register.name: Agricultural high schools and three mini hydropower plants
register.detail: Signed 10 November 2025, Conakry · two EBID loans · €28.28 million for four agricultural high schools · €95.16 million for three plants of 27.6 MW in all
register.note: Four agricultural lycées modernised; hydropower in the Senegal River basin
register.text: Modernises four agricultural high schools and builds three small hydropower plants for rural electrification. It serves education and energy.
by: ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development

register.name: Rural and urban drinking water in Upper Guinea and Forest Guinea
register.detail: Signed 9 August 2024, Conakry · two EBID loans · $34.3 million for 150 boreholes and 100 water systems · $28.4 million for Beyla, Fria and Koubia
register.note: Boreholes with hand pumps and piped systems; 205,204 people in three towns by 2035
register.text: Two loans for drinking water: 150 boreholes with hand pumps and 100 supply systems in Upper and Forest Guinea, and piped water for 205,204 people in Beyla, Fria and Koubia. It serves water.
by: ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development

register.name: 225 kV Guinea–Mali electricity interconnection, additional financing
register.detail: Approved 10 December 2025, Abidjan · African Development Fund · loan of about $22 million and grant of $3.79 million
register.note: Cost overruns and about 37,500 new connections
register.text: Completes the Guinean side of the line to Mali, whose cost rises from $346 million to $372 million, and adds about 37,500 new electricity connections. It serves energy.

register.name: Industrial development and SME resilience
register.detail: Approved June 2024 · African Development Fund loan · Transition Support Facility
register.note: Industrial development and the resilience of small and medium enterprises
register.text: A loan to support industrial development and make small and medium enterprises more resilient. It serves livelihood.

register.name: AFG Bank Guinée, SME loan and trade finance guarantee
register.detail: Proparco · Published 13 October 2026 · €35 million senior loan for SMEs · €25 million trade finance guarantee facility
register.note: 3,766 direct and indirect jobs to be sustained or created
register.text: Lets AFG Bank Guinée double its SME loan portfolio from €60 million to €120 million by 2027, and covers the international trade instruments it issues. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Vista Gui, loan for small businesses
register.detail: IFC · Approved 27 March 2026 · signed 30 March 2026 · five-year senior loan, in US dollars · pending disbursement
register.note: At least a quarter for businesses owned or led by women
register.text: A senior loan to the Guinean subsidiary of Vista Group, to increase access to longer-term financing for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises. It serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Fermav Industries (SONOCO Group), integrated poultry
register.detail: IFC · Approved 17 March 2026 · signed 28 March 2026 · senior loan of up to $20 million · $49 million investment programme
register.note: About 400 direct and nearly 3,500 indirect jobs expected
register.text: Finances a greenfield poultry operation in Guinea, from feed production and hatcheries to processing and distribution, with a hatchery near Kindia, a slaughterhouse in Massayah and a feed mill in Sanoyah. It serves the food standard and is to reduce the dependence of Guinea on imports.

register.name: BCI Guinea, loan for small and medium enterprises
register.detail: Proparco · Signed 8 September 2025 in Conakry · senior loan · Choose Africa
register.note: With technical assistance for an environmental and social management system
register.text: A senior loan to Banque pour le Commerce et l’Industrie Guinée, fully dedicated to financing small and medium-sized enterprises. It serves the livelihood standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Iron Mountain
items.label: High-grade iron ore at Simandou
items.text: One of the world’s largest high-grade deposits, exporting since November 2025 toward about 120 million tonnes a year.

items.name: The Bauxite
items.label: The world’s largest bauxite reserves
items.text: The ore of aluminium, already Guinea’s leading export.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Rivers already give nearly nine tenths of the power: the water tower of West Africa.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 40.6% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: AMIMA
items.text: A Guinean company, founded in 2017, that distributes fresh fruit and vegetables by connecting growers directly to organised buyers such as large restaurants, hotels and mining bases. It works with about a hundred producers in some twenty prefectures.

items.name: Fermav Industries
items.text: A greenfield poultry company of the Guinean group SONOCO, covering feed production, hatcheries and farming through to processing and distribution, to reduce the dependence of Guinea on imported chicken. IFC lends about $20 million; about 400 direct and nearly 3,500 indirect jobs are expected.

items.name: SOIK Corporation (SPAQ)
items.text: A Japanese company whose SPAQ technology connects a dedicated app to a portable ultrasound device to modernise antenatal care. A pilot launched in Conakry on 16 June 2026 with UNFPA, funded by Japan with $393,333, is to equip 10 health facilities in remote areas; more than 5,000 pregnant women are expected to benefit.

items.name: Labtani
items.text: A Guinean e-health start-up launched in 2025, whose app gives patients remote consultations and lets them book laboratory tests. It had been downloaded more than a hundred times on the Play Store by January 2026.

items.name: Finadev
items.text: A microfinance institution set up in 1998, in the pan-African Finafrica network since 2019 and one of the five leading players in microfinance in Guinea, lending to small businesses. Proparco signed a €2 million ARIZ portfolio guarantee with it on 22 November 2023.
